input: n is a nonnegative integer. edges contains E directed valid vertex pairs on IDs 0 through n-1 and describes a directed acyclic graph. Parallel edges are allowed; self-loops/cycles are outside the domain. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt; separately declared probabilities are finite primitive Number.
return: Fresh length-n array of fresh sorted rows, where row[v] contains exactly all distinct vertices with a directed path of positive length to v, in strictly increasing numeric order.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and edge rows remain unchanged. Local adjacency, indegrees, sets and head-cursor queue are private; output rows are fresh and independent. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Indegrees count every edge occurrence and cannot become negative. Numeric sorting differences lie between -(n-1) and n-1. DAG topological processing guarantees each source ancestor set is complete before propagation and prevents a node becoming its own ancestor. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n + E + n*E + A*log(n+1) + 1) time and O(n + E + A + 1) auxiliary/output space, where A is total ancestor incidences. Counts include set propagation for every edge, sorted output copies/workspace, adjacency and retained queue. Hash-table and comparison-sort assumptions remain explicit. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.
